Expires: 10/18/2026 Location: Monroeville, PennsylvaniaJob Title: Intern - Business Systems AdministratorStatus: InternHourly Rate: $28Job SummaryAs a Business Systems Administrator Intern at BPMI, you will be responsible for assisting in the administration, maintenance, and support of BPMI business systems (e.g. Oracle Fusion Cloud) to promote reliable operations, effective security and internal controls, accurate information, and efficient business processes. Duties:Assist with basic maintenance and administration of BPMI business systems, including enabling and disabling users, managing role permissions, and scheduling reports under close supervision.Support system upgrades by executing test cases, documenting results, and assisting with rollout activities under significant oversight.Assist with system configuration activities by documenting configuration changes and tracking work performed by third-party consultants under supervision.Help coordinate user support activities, including answering basic system usage questions, assisting with troubleshooting, and updating system process documentation.Gather documentation and system information to support internal and external audit requests under significant oversight.Support updating procedures, user guides, training materials, and other documentation to reflect approved system or process changes.Participate in department initiatives related to process improvement, operational effectiveness, and system changes in a supporting role.The essential duties identified are representative but are not intended to be an exhaustive or inclusive list of all the responsibilities of the position.What You Can Expect:A culture that values people through recognition of accomplishments, work-life balance, and a sense of community.A diverse group of talented individuals working toward the common goal of supporting the United States Navy in their pursuit of national security.Competitive and attractive pay and benefits with a stable organization.Opportunities to participate in BPMI sponsored committees and clubs, each with their own mission and purpose.Career advancement and professional development programs.Minimum Job Requirements:Enrolled in Management Information Systems, Business Analytics, Computer Science, Computer Information Systems, Business Intelligence, Information Systems / Technology or related undergraduate degree program from an accredited college or university.Minimum of six (6) semesters completed prior to your internship (~90 credits).Requires a security clearance; however, all qualified candidates will be considered regardless of their current clearance status. The ability to obtain and maintain a Department of Energy security clearance is required.Preferred Job Requirements:Minimum GPA of 3.0 preferred; actively pursuing a degree in a related field.Working knowledge of Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), Outlook, and other common business applications.Basic knowledge of Oracle Fusion Cloud (Enterprise Resource Management, Supply Chain Management, and Human Capital Management)Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, including the ability to write clear technical documentation.Able to work independently and as part of a team, with strong attention to detail, deadlines, and quality.Demonstrated ability to build positive working relationships and adapt to evolving project requirements while following organizational policies and procedures.Fundamental understanding of business processes and systems, with strong analytical and problem-solving skills and the ability to prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.Why BPMI?Bechtel Plant Machinery, Inc. (BPMI) is a prime contractor for the Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program (NNPP). BPMI is involved in the design, purchase, quality control, and delivery of major propulsion plant components for installation in nuclear-powered aircraft carriers, submarines, and prototype plants for the U.S. Navy. Teamwork, cooperation, and the pursuit of excellence have been the driving forces behind the growth and success of BPMI. For more information, visit www.bpmionline.com. BPMI is a drug-free workplace. Candidates accepting a job offer will be required to pass a pre-placement drug screening and background investigation. As an employee, you will be required to receive and maintain a security clearance from the United States Department of Energy in order to meet requirements for access to sensitive information or matter. U.S. citizenship is a requirement for security clearance applicants. All employees are subject to being randomly selected for drug testing without advance notification. jobs.feedName: Andrew J. Anagnost College of Engineering and Computer Science
jobs.title: Product Engineer Intern at OpenGov
jobs.description: Employer: OpenGov Expires: 10/18/2026 About the RoleOpenGov is looking for Product Engineer Interns who are eager to learn what it means to own a product — from customer discovery through delivery. This internship is built around a new kind of role born from AI's ability to handle execution work that once required multiple specialists. What AI cannot do is decide what matters, talk to customers, make the right call in ambiguous situations, or own whether a product succeeds. That is what Product Engineers learn to do — and this internship is where that journey starts.This role is first and foremost about developing product thinking — not becoming a developer. The best interns will be the ones who grow genuinely curious about customers: who they are, what they actually need, and what outcomes depend on solving their problems. The engineering side — using AI-native tooling to write code, build interfaces — is a skill you will be introduced to and encouraged to develop. It is a career accelerator, not a day-one requirement.If you have a background or strong interest in product management, UX design, engineering, or some combination — and you want real ownership of a problem rather than a slide deck — this internship is for you."Product Engineer" is two words — but the first word is the one that matters most. The second is how you get there. The 10-week internship will run from June 7, 2027 through August 13, 2027. What You'll Work OnA scoped product problem: a defined set of customers, problems, and outcomes — sized for a 10–12 week engagement with real impact.Customer discovery: you will conduct or observe customer conversations and translate what you learn into product decisions.User experience flows: you will define interaction patterns within an existing design system and validate them with users.AI-assisted delivery: using AI-native tooling, you will move from intent to spec to working prototype — supported by your team, but accountable for the output.Metrics: you will define what success looks like for your area and track it throughout the internship. How AI Works in This RoleAI-native tooling handles a significant portion of what product managers and designers have historically spent their time on. As an intern, you will be hands-on with these tools from day one:Spec writing: AI drafts the first spec from your intent statement. You learn to review, sharpen, and own what gets built.UX design: AI generates mockups from the design system based on your flow definitions. You make the product decisions within it.Research synthesis: AI clusters and themes interview notes and support data. You interpret what it means and make the call.Release content: AI generates release notes and enablement materials from shipped features. You review and refine them.Test coverage: AI generates test cases from acceptance criteria. You learn to write criteria precise enough to verify.What AI does not do: understand your customers, make the call on what matters, own the outcome, or build the cross-functional trust that makes things ship. That is the job — and what you will be learning. Key ResponsibilitiesParticipate in customer discovery conversations; synthesize what you hear into defensible product decisions.Define user experience flows and interaction patterns within the existing design system.Write intent documents that AI tooling can execute against; review AI-generated specs for accuracy and completeness.Partner with your engineering and product mentor to resolve ambiguity in real time during the development cycle.Track adoption and usage metrics for your scoped area; use them to drive iteration.Present your product area and findings in a final intern showcase — covering the customer problem, what you built, and what you would do next.Surface gaps, risks, and unanswered questions proactively; don't wait to be asked. Qualifications & What We're Looking ForCurrently pursuing a degree in computer science, information systems, product design, HCI, business, or a closely adjacent field — or equivalent self-directed experience.Genuine curiosity about customers and why products succeed or fail; you find yourself asking "who is this for and does it actually solve their problem?"Strong written communication: you can articulate a product decision clearly enough that an engineer and a designer walk away aligned.Comfort with ambiguity and speed: you make reasonable decisions with incomplete information rather than waiting for certainty.Willingness to grow into code fluency using AI-native tooling — you don't need to arrive as a developer, but you must be willing to get there.Prior exposure to product management, UX design, software development, or customer research is a plus — in any form (coursework, projects, prior internships, side work).Familiarity with design tools (Figma, etc.) or development tooling is welcome but not required. CompensationBoston, MA: $30 per hour

jobs.description: Employer: Virginia Department of Transportation Expires: 10/19/2026 Kick-start your career with VDOT! jobs.title: AI Intern at Graco Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Graco Inc. Expires: 10/19/2026 The AI Engineer Intern position is responsible for assisting in the development, testing, and deployment of Generative AI solutions in collaboration with product managers, software engineers, and cloud architects. The individual in this position will have foundational knowledge of Large Language Models (LLMs) and generative AI technologies with hands-on experience in implementing AI-powered business applications. This role supports the technical implementation of Gen AI solutions on cloud platforms and contributes to solving real-world business problems through innovative LLM-based applications. What You Will Do: Generative AI Development· Participate in the full GenAI development lifecycle including prompt engineering, model fine-tuning, testing, and deployment.· Assist in developing and maintaining scalable LLM-based applications and generative AI solutions.· Implement and optimize prompts for various business use cases including content generation, document processing, and intelligent automation.· Support integration of foundation models (GPT, Claude, LLaMA) and custom LLMs into cloud-based production systems.· Deploy and manage AI models on cloud platforms (AWS Bedrock, OCI AI Services) to deliver business solutions.· Document prompt strategies, model configurations, and deployment workflows to ensure reproducibility and adhere to quality standards. Cross-Functional Partnership· Work with business stakeholders to understand requirements and design LLM-powered solutions for specific use cases.· Collaborate closely with cloud engineers, architects, and cross-functional teams to implement GenAI applications.· Research and experiment with the latest generative AI models, frameworks, and cloud AI services to improve business solutions.· Stay up to date with emerging LLM technologies, prompt engineering techniques, and cloud AI platform capabilities. What You Will Bring:· Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, or related field.· Understanding of Large Language Models (LLMs), generative AI concepts, and foundation model architectures.· Proficiency in Python and familiarity with GenAI frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Transformers).· Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, OCI) and AI services (AWS Bedrock, OCI AI Services, Azure OpenAI).· Knowledge of prompt engineering techniques, model fine-tuning, and LLM optimization strategies.· Understanding of API integration, microservices architecture, and cloud-native development.· Strong problem-solving skills with focus on business use case implementation.· Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.· Familiarity with version control systems (Git) and cloud development practices. Accelerators:· Experience with advanced prompt engineering, RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) implementations, and vector databases.· Knowledge of cloud infrastructure (AWS EC2, Lambda, OCI Compute) and serverless architectures for AI applications.· Familiarity with LLMOps tools (MLflow, Weights & Biases) and model monitoring in cloud environments.· Experience with containerization (Docker, Kubernetes) for deploying GenAI applications at scale.· Understanding of AI governance, model safety, and responsible AI practices.· Experience working in an Agile environment with cloud-first development approaches.· Previous projects involving business process automation using generative AI.

You will have the opportunity to discover where your strengths and interests lie and how you can best apply your skills. The work environment is collegial; and there is significant, on-going contact between senior and junior staff.The CandidateThe ideal candidates will be pursuing, and possess:An undergraduate degree in a quantitative discipline (e.g. economics, computer science, data science, and mathematics), with strong academic performance. Successful applicants typically have a GPA of 3.7 or higher (based on a 4.0 scale).Great teamwork and leadership skills. Our project work is done almost exclusively on teams, so it’s critical that our EA interns work well with others.Intellectual curiosity and creativity. We are looking for candidates who consistently want to learn more and approach problems with creativity.A high degree of ownership and commitment. Successful EA interns are committed to delivering their best work product, taking ownership of their work, and engaging in excellent client services.Strong communication skills.Additionally, we look for candidates who:Have completed or will complete a course with a climate or energy focus.To Be Considered for the Energy Analyst Intern Position:Please submit the following materials as soon as possible via the application below.Cover LetterResumeTranscript(s) (unofficial copies accepted)To streamline the process, please use your school-issued email address on your application.The anticipated base gross salary for this position in Boston, MA is $1,850.00 per week.EQUAL OPPORTUNITYThe Brattle Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. jobs.description: Employer: Novonesis Expires: 10/20/2026 Interested in a career that matters? jobs.description: Employer: Quantum Signal AI Expires: 10/21/2026 This is a paid internship. Compensation for this position begins at $29.00 per hour.Role Summary: Quantum Signal AI (QSAI) is looking for a Software Engineering Intern – Tools and Prototypes to help develop engineering tooling and prototype software for the summer of 2027. Our applications range from specialized engineering tools to prototypes for advanced vehicle features that are used by engineers, researchers, and designers at Ford and QSAI. Interns will work alongside experienced engineers throughout the software development lifecycle and gain hands-on experience solving real engineering problems in a fast-paced R&D environment. A standout candidate will have experience in compiled languages (C++, Go, etc.), scripting languages (Python, JavaScript, etc.), web development, and software projects outside of an academic setting. We value the ability to quickly learn new technology to meet changing requirements, so a desire to learn is important! Location: Saline, Michigan (In-person). Our “historic schoolhouse” office supports hands-on collaboration, mentorship, and real-time problem solving. What You’ll Do (Essential Functions): Contribute to projects across the full Software Development Lifecycle, from design and implementation, to testing and release management Collaborate within varied project teams to develop tooling to improve engineering workflows Translate ideas, specifications, and/or requirements into high-quality implementations Tackle the challenges of learning, integrating, and leveraging a range of software tools and technologies as needed Develop documentation for software, processes, and projects Create and maintain build processes and CI/CD pipelines What You’ll Bring (Minimum Requirements): Current enrollment in an undergraduate degree-seeking program, pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related field Maintaining student status for the entire duration of the internship, including the academic term immediately following the internship Strong understanding of computer science fundamentals including data structures, algorithms, object-oriented programming, debugging, networking, and file systems Previous work/internship or academic club experience developing software Proficiency developing software in a compiled language (C++, Go, etc.) Experience with scripting languages (Python, JavaScript, etc.) Experience working in both Linux- and Windows-based environments Familiarity with web development (HTML, CSS, JS, etc.) Bonus Points For: Coursework or equivalent experience in operating systems, databases, compilers, concurrency, and other high level computer science topics Experience with REST APIs, either through integrating with existing APIs or designing APIs for downstream consumers Experience with modern web development frameworks and technologies (Node.js, React, Typescript, Flask, etc.) Experience with cloud-based development/deployment via GCP or equivalent cloud provider Experience integrating Identity and Access Management (IAM) solutions into an application (Microsoft Entra, RBAC, MSAL, authentication and authorization APIs) You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you are excited about this role and think you can bring value to Quantum Signal AI, we encourage you to apply! What You’ll Get: Frequent collaboration with a diverse set of teams at QSAI A rare level of work variety and hands-on experience A relaxed, fun community and environment in which to solve interesting problems Opportunity to participate in a 401(k) savings plan Ford AX-Plan vehicle discounts Mentorship-focused learning that emphasizes engineering fundamentals, hands-on problem solving, and understanding the underlying principles behind the systems we build. Other perks to fuel creativity such as an on-site gymnasium, free drinks and snacks, and a variety of optional team activities Candidates for positions with Quantum Signal AI must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required at the time of hire. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. About QSAI: Founded in 1999, Quantum Signal grew up developing intelligent algorithms and AI. As our engineering R&D services expanded, we later sharpened our focus on applications and technology related to mobility, sensing, perception, autonomy, and simulation. In 2019 we became Quantum Signal AI, a subsidiary of Ford Motor developing technologies to advance their R&D efforts. We build solutions to enhance the capability, robustness, safety, and acceptance of intelligent ground vehicles in an effort to make transportation more effective and efficient for all. While AI is part of our name, our internship program emphasizes building fundamental engineering knowledge, analytical thinking, and practical problem-solving skills. We want interns to understand how and why systems work through hands-on experience, mentorship, and experimentation, rather than simply relying on tools to provide answers. Our HQ in the historic Union School in Saline, MI is the perfect playground to develop this cutting-edge technology and we’re always looking for smart folks who like new challenges, learning new skills, and technical variety.

jobs.title: Internship: Transportation/Public Works at Hennepin County
jobs.description: Employer: Hennepin County Expires: 10/21/2026 Internship: Transportation/Public WorksSalary$22.50 - $26.21 HourlyJob TypeInternshipJob Number26TRNS832FM210Closing Date10/26/2026 11:59 PM CentralDescriptionHennepin County Public Works is seeking to fill multiple non-benefit earning internships. These positions will be a part of the Design, Bridge, Construction, Planning, Traffic and Asset Management divisions. Current Hennepin County employees who refer a candidate hired into an open competitive position may be eligible for a $500 referral bonus. For more information visit employee referral program.Location and hours:These positions are hybrid and will be performed both on-site at the Public Works Facility located at 1600 Prairie Drive in Medina, MN 55340 or in a field environment within Hennepin County, and remote as job duties require. The Public Works Facility in Medina is not accessible by public transportation. These positions will start in May/June 2027 and last through August 2027 with flexible start and end dates. Interns are scheduled to work 40 hours per week during the summer, Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. with some flexibility on work schedules. When school is in session, interns may work 5-10 hours per week depending on student interest and availability. While these positions are designated as hybrid, based on current requirements hires must reside in or relocate to Minnesota or Wisconsin. About these position types:These positions are limited duration, non-benefit earning internships.These positions are internally classified as an Intern II.Click here to view the job classification specification. Applicants are encouraged to attach a current resume.The responsibilities of each position include but are not limited to the following:Transportation Design Division: The preferred candidate will have a strong interest in transportation design and will be responsible for the following tasks:Support design teams with CAD drawings, plan preparation, modeling, and basic engineering calculations.Collaborate with teams across the design division - including transportation, water resources, traffic, bidding, and specifications on various engineering tasks.Participate in field visits, job shadowing, and attending project coordination meetings to gain exposure to Public Works and Hennepin County operations.Assist with completing an audit of the County’s municipal stormwater program.Contribute to research on a relevant engineering topic and present key findings to the design division.Develop hands-on experience in design workflows and present key internship takeaways and acquired skills at the conclusion of the program.Support project managers and design staff through data gathering, documentation, and coordination activities. Transportation Bridge: The preferred candidate will have a strong interest in bridge work and will be responsible for the following tasks: Support the development and modification of technical drawings and documents for bridges and retaining walls.Review and interpret engineering plans, details, codes, and standards to assist project teams.Assist with quantity take-offs, cost estimates, and engineering calculations under close supervision.Contribute to Hennepin County’s annual bridge inspection program.Conduct research using technical drawings, standards, and engineering references to support project documentation.Aid in preparing computations, technical reports, and drafting tasks.Update and maintain the GIS database for retaining wall inventory. Transportation Construction: The preferred candidate will have a strong interest in construction and transportation and will be responsible for the following tasks:Assist in construction surveying, inspection activities, and contract administration.Support materials testing and soils investigations under the guidance of engineering staff.Perform and verify quantity calculations to support project documentation and cost tracking.Enter data into software applications and generate required outputs.Document field activities, summarize findings, and assist in routine report preparation.Contribute to data management by maintaining accurate project records and activity logs.Collaborate with project teams to ensure quality control and adherence to construction standards. Transportation Planning: The preferred candidate will have a strong interest in transportation planning, CAD work, and compiling data and will be responsible for the following tasks:Assist with developing CAD drawings for pavement restriping concepts.Compile quantity takeoffs from completed plans in preparation for year-end metrics reporting.Researching low-cost, high-impact safety improvements that can be utilized across the county to improve safety for all road users.Conduct data analysis, create crash diagrams, and contribute toward before-after-research involving transportation safety in Hennepin County.Assist with GIS mapping, crash data analysis, and application development for the upcoming Regional Solicitation and Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Solicitation.Support the Capital Project Prioritization process with work tasks such as updating guidelines, developing materials for the Technical Work Group, and preparing documents for project scoping.Archive project documentation for the Capital Budget preparation.Transportation Traffic: The preferred candidate will have a strong interest in traffic work and will be responsible for the following tasks:Collect, process, and analyze traffic data. Perform traffic detection accuracy validation.Monitor real-time traffic conditions through traffic cameras.Observe operation of traffic signal detection and controller systems.Assist in the maintenance of coordinated signal timing operations.Assist in organizing documents and database related to the operation of traffic signals.Create sketches of intersections and collect measurements of turn lanes. Support IT to help resolve communication network issues.Public Works Asset Management: The preferred candidate will have a strong interest in tracking, managing, and making improvements to transportation and environmental infrastructure, and will be responsible for the following tasks:Assist with plan production using OpenRoads and support project estimates, specifications, and related documentation.Collect and verify transportation, environmental, and pavement asset data in the field using GPS, cellular, or vehicle technology, following established guidelines.Support GIS mapping and data management tasks, including creating dashboards, static maps, and conducting data analysis.Compile, process, and document physical and digital data to develop metrics, perform cost analyses, and prepare routine reports.Gain hands-on experience within the Asset Management Division through fieldwork, job shadowing, and presenting key internship learnings at the conclusion of the program.Need to have: Must be in one of the following:Enrollment for the 2026-2027 academic school year in a vocational/technical or undergraduate degree program in civil engineering, construction, geography, Geographic Information System (GIS), land surveying/highway engineering technology, data science, urban planning/studies or another related field.Recent graduate (within 6 months) in a vocational/technical or an undergraduate degree program in civil engineering, construction, geography, Geographic Information System (GIS), land surveying/highway engineering technology, data science, urban planning/studies or another related field.A valid driver's license and the ability to obtain a Hennepin County driver's permit.Reliable internet connection and self-support hybrid office space.Nice to have:Experience: Troubleshooting basic computer issues with efficiency and accuracy.Working with Adobe Acrobat, Adobe Creative Suite, ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS Pro, CAD, Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Access), Microstation/AutoCAD, and/or Synchro/SimTraffic.Knowledge of:Math functions such as arithmetic, algebra, and geometry.Python, ArcPy or Arcade languages. Ability to:Walk on uneven terrain; bend and stoop; work outdoors in all types of weather conditions.Communicate with staff at all levels of the organization, in person, via email and phone. If you have questions, contact:Talent Acquisition divisionHennepin County Human Resources departmentSubmit a request at hennepin.us/ask-hror 612-348-7855Internship2000

jobs.feedName: Andrew J. Anagnost College of Engineering and Computer Science
jobs.title: C++ Software Developer Intern at Scalp Trade
jobs.description: Employer: Scalp Trade Expires: 10/21/2026 We are seeking a driven and intellectually curious C++ Software Developer Intern to join our dynamic trading firm. This is an exceptional opportunity to gain hands-on experience building high-performance trading systems while contributing meaningfully to our operations. You will work closely with experienced engineers in a mentorship-rich environment, learning cutting-edge low-latency systems design, trading infrastructure, and modern C++ development practices. This internship is designed to accelerate your growth as a software engineer while you help develop tools and strategies that directly impact our trading operations. If you thrive on learning, enjoy solving complex technical problems, and want to understand how financial technology works at scale, this is the role for you. Key Responsibilities & Learning Objectives Develop and Optimize Components: Under mentor guidance, design and implement features for automated trading systems, with emphasis on understanding the 'why' behind architectural decisions in high-performance environments.Collaborative Development: Contribute to core trading platform enhancements alongside senior engineers, learning best practices for low-latency, distributed systems.Code Quality & Design: Learn and apply SOLID principles, modern C++ patterns, and system design concepts through hands-on code reviews and pair programming sessions.Performance Analysis: Participate in profiling and optimizing trading system components; understand tuning techniques for real-time operations.Documentation & Knowledge Sharing: Document code, design decisions, and lessons learned to build your technical communication skills.Problem-Solving: Work on well-scoped technical challenges that build your analytical and debugging skills in a production environment. Required Skills & QualificationsStrong Foundation in C++: Solid grasp of C++ fundamentals (STL, memory management, move semantics, templates). Production experience not required; demonstrated projects or coursework show readiness.Core CS Fundamentals: Comfortable with data structures, algorithms, and basic systems concepts (threading, process synchronization).Quick Learner: Able to rapidly pick up new tools, libraries, and frameworks with minimal guidance.Linux Familiarity: Comfortable working in Linux environments; shell scripting and command-line tools are a plus.Collaborative Mindset: Excellent communication skills; eager to learn from mentors and ask clarifying questions. Preferred Skills Multi-threading Experience: Practical familiarity with concurrent programming, thread safety, and synchronization primitives.Network Programming: Exposure to socket programming, TCP/IP, or distributed system basics.Additional Languages: Proficiency in Python, C#, or other systems languages broadens your perspective.Financial Markets Interest: Curiosity about trading, equities, options, or how financial markets work—we teach the rest.Database Exposure: Familiarity with SQL or understanding of how databases store and retrieve data at scale.Version Control & Tooling: Experience with Git, debugging tools (gdb, valgrind), or profilers (perf, flamegraph). Personal Attributes Intellectual Curiosity: Genuine interest in understanding how systems work, from code to infrastructure to business outcomes.Growth Mindset: Embrace challenges and feedback as opportunities to learn. We expect you to grow significantly over the internship.Ownership & Initiative: Proactive in seeking learning opportunities and taking on well-scoped responsibilities with minimal oversight.Adaptability: Comfortable with ambiguity and rapid changes; thriving in a fast-paced, high-performance environment.Collaborative Problem-Solving: Strong analytical skills with a preference for brainstorming and learning from teammates.Passion for Technology: Excitement about staying current with modern C++ and high-performance systems. What You'll GainHands-On Production Experience: Work in a real, production trading environment—not a sandbox. Your code runs strategies that generate revenue.Mentorship from Experts: Learn directly from senior engineers with deep expertise in low-latency systems, C++, and financial technology.Comprehensive Technical Knowledge: Understand high-performance systems design, from kernel tuning to network stack optimization.Career Acceleration: Build a portfolio of impactful projects and establish relationships with leaders in fintech.Potential for Conversion: Strong performers are considered for full-time roles upon graduation or at the conclusion of the internship. Compensation: This internship is paid at $7,000 per month for the program.

jobs.title: Engineering Intern- Summer 2027 at Medtronic
jobs.description: Employer: Medtronic Expires: 10/21/2026 CAREERS THAT CHANGE LIVES Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact. Our summer internships are full-time (40 hours/week), paid positions lasting 10-11 weeks. We offer competitive compensation, educational and social programming throughout the summer, as well as housing assistance and relocation support for eligible interns. Engineering Intern Opportunities for Students Interns may support one or more engineering areas based on business need, candidate background, and location availability. Examples of work in each area are listed below. Research & Development Engineering Support design, development, analysis, and testing of engineering solutions during research and product development phases. Contribute to system integration, verification, validation, risk analysis, and data-driven evaluation efforts. Support safety testing, regulatory compliance, and transfer of products from development into manufacturing. jobs.title: Virtual Design & Construction Intern at Pieper Electric, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Pieper Electric, Inc. - Pieper Electric, Inc Expires: 10/22/2026 Job DescriptionPosition Summary BIM is something we use. VDC is how we use digital information and technology to plan, coordinate, and improve how we build. As a Virtual Design & Construction Intern at Pieper Electric, you will learn how Building Information Modeling (BIM) supports the larger Virtual Design and Construction (VDC) process. You will gain hands-on experience using digital construction tools that support planning and field execution through model navigation, clash detection, constructability reviews, layout, and prefabrication. Working alongside BIM Specialists, Detailing Specialists, Project Managers, field leaders, and other project partners, you will help develop and coordinate constructible electrical models and drawings that connect design information to how work is planned, fabricated, laid out, and installed in the field. This internship is designed for students who enjoy technology, problem-solving, spatial thinking, and seeing how things are built. You do not need to know every BIM platform before joining us. We are looking for students who are curious, detail-oriented, willing to learn, and interested in understanding how digital models can be used to solve real construction challenges. Interns will receive guidance, feedback, and opportunities to take ownership of defined assignments under appropriate supervision. Values and Ways of Working At Pieper Electric, we believe in the Power to Serve and the Pursuit of Excellence. Our values, a Servant’s Heart, Wisdom, Integrity, Courage, Humility, and Passion, guide how we learn, collaborate, support the field, and serve our customers and teammates. As an intern, you will be encouraged to ask questions, share ideas, take initiative, and learn from experienced professionals while contributing to a safe and respectful team environment. Essential Responsibilities Safety and Field Engagement Complete required safety training and follow all company, customer, and jobsite requirements.Participate in supervised jobsite and prefabrication shop visits to understand how model information translates to installation.Learn how BIM supports safer planning, constructability, layout, prefabrication, and field execution.Promptly communicate safety concerns, field observations, or differences between modeled conditions and field conditions.BIM Modeling and Model Navigation Learn to navigate, review, create, and update 3D electrical models using Revit and other company BIM platforms.Assist with modeling electrical systems and components in support of coordination, constructability, prefabrication, layout, and installation.Review project drawings, specifications, submittals, and other available project information to support accurate model development.Update models as design information, coordination decisions, and field conditions change.Prepare model views and information that help project and field teams understand planned installation.Coordination, Clash Detection and Constructability Participate in BIM coordination and constructability reviews with project teams and trade partners.Learn how electrical systems are coordinated with architectural, structural, mechanical, plumbing, fire protection, and other building systems.Assist with identifying, documenting, and resolving clashes or spatial conflicts before installation.Review modeled routing and installation approaches with constructability, access, sequencing, and field execution in mind.Support approved model revisions resulting from coordination and constructability reviews.Detailing, Layout and Field Execution Assist with coordinated drawings, installation details, layouts, point drawings, and other field-ready information generated from or supported by BIM.Learn to interpret electrical symbols, one-lines, schedules, construction jobs.title: Structural Engineer Internship at GRAEF
jobs.description: Employer: GRAEF Expires: 10/22/2026 GRAEF, a leading U.S. consulting firm, has been providing exceptional careers and quality engineering, planning and design services to our clients since 1961. We recognize that the best workplaces are filled with technically excellent, innovative, creative, and highly motivated people. GRAEF is more than just a business. We are a committed employer and community member. We invest in our employees as we do our clients, providing a challenging and rewarding environment where you can grow both personally and professionally. GRAEF values exciting work and lasting relationships; we embody values that speak to loyalty, service, quality and integrity; and we strive to grow with these ideas leading the way. We’re looking for people who agree that in addition to technical excellence, it’s all about relationships! We have an exciting Internship opportunity available for a student pursuing their degree in Structural Engineering, with an interest in either structural design of buildings or bridges. In this role, you will have the opportunity to work in a collaborative learning environment on a wide variety of bridge projects, from new build to reconstruction projects, and a variety of building projects including healthcare, higher-education, multi-family, hospitality, commercial, industrial and renovation projects. This exciting internship is available in our new Chicago office located at the President's Plaza, beginning in the summer of 2027. As a Structural Engineer Intern at GRAEF, enjoy responsibilities like:Learn design and specifications for a variety of building structures.Assemble design documentation, reports, and quantity calculations for checking.Use of Revit for construction documentation and coordination with project team members.Learn design and specifications for transportation structures, including highway and railroad bridges, retaining walls and box culverts under the supervision of the lead structural engineer, per DOT requirements.Assemble design documentation, reports, and quantity calculations for checking.Perform structural inspection of bridges and highway structures.Perform work as part of a team, in accordance with project budget and schedule under supervision.To be considered for our Structural Engineer Internship position, we are seeking candidates who meet the following basic qualifications:Pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering with a Structural emphasis in course work.Pursuing a Master’s degree in Structural Engineering would be a plus.Internship experience in structural building or bridge design/bridge inspection is preferred. Ability to grasp new concepts and eager to learn new things.Enjoy a balance of independent tasks and working with a project team.Hourly pay rate is between $22-$24/hour.As an Intern at GRAEF, we are proud to offer you: Embed yourself in the community by participating in numerous outside activities that GRAEF endorses and supportsOffice location is close to many amenities, including onsite fitness center and free parkingRetirement Savings PlanImmersive Mentorship ProgramRobust Workplace Wellness ProgramSocial and Networking opportunitiesA team atmosphere dedicated to open communication and collaborationFlexible ScheduleCasual DressAn Equal Opportunity Employer/Affirmative Action Employer - Disabled/Vets

jobs.title: Hardware Test Engineering Co-Op at Delta Faucet Company
jobs.description: Employer: Delta Faucet Company - Delta Faucet HQ- Indianapolis, IN Expires: 10/23/2026 At Delta Faucet, we are committed to transforming everyday experiences with water through innovative products and exceptional service. As a leader in the plumbing industry, we take pride in our dedication to quality, sustainability, and customer satisfaction. We believe that diverse perspectives strengthen our mission to create solutions that inspire and elevate the lives of all our customers. We welcome individuals from all backgrounds to join us on this journey toward inclusivity and excellence. Your Role at Delta FaucetDelta Faucet Company has an opportunity for a Hardware Engineering Co-op to join our Connected Water Team to help deliver the next generation of product features and technology to our customers. In this role, you will support the development of new digital products through hands-on work with embedded systems and real product hardware. You will spend most of your days in the lab doing hands-on and varied tasks: soldering and reworking assemblies, programming and bringing up circuit boards, running electrical and functional tests, laying out PCBs, and keeping our engineering lab and its equipment running as smoothly as possible.You will report to the engineering manager and sit with the project teams, not apart from them. Within your first few weeks you will be assigned specific tasks, projects, and test processes to own — meaning you make the calls there, you document how it works, and you are the person others ask about it. When you find a better way to do something, we want to hear it, and we will give you a straight answer either way. Every part of the role is scoped so that the skills you leave with — test methodology, debugging discipline, documentation, lab ownership — are the ones that help you with the rest of your college work and prepare you for your future career. Responsibilities:Build and ReworkSolder, rework, and modify through-hole and surface-mount assemblies for prototypes, test fixtures, and engineering samples.Assemble and wire test fixtures, harnesses, and benchtop setups from schematics and written instructions.Program, flash, and bring up circuit boards; verify power rails, signal integrity, and basic functionality on new builds.Test and DebugExecute electrical, functional, and reliability tests on products and subassemblies, and record results accurately.Investigate test failures: reproduce the issue, isolate it to a component or subsystem, and document what you found so an engineer can act on it.Write and maintain basic test scripts and data-logging routines to automate repetitive measurements.Operate and troubleshoot standard bench equipment — oscilloscopes, DMMs, power supplies, function generators, data acquisition systems, environmental chambers.Design SupportProduce PCB layouts for test fixtures, adapter boards, and design revisions under engineering guidance.Review schematics and layouts for manufacturability and testability, and raise concerns before boards are ordered.Suggest product and process improvements based on what you observe on the benchLab and Calibration OwnershipOrganize and manage the engineering lab: equipment inventory, tool and fixture storage, consumable stock, workspace layout, and bench readiness.Run the equipment calibration program — track calibration due dates, coordinate with vendors, maintain certificates, and keep instruments in a known-good state.Establish and document standard operating procedures for test setups, lab safety, and equipment use so results are repeatable across people and across time.Maintain clear technical documentation: test reports, procedures, wiring diagrams, bring-up notes, and change records.Where this goesWe treat this co-op as the first step in a career here, not a temporary set of hands. The scope is designed to grow with you:In your first term, you will learn our products, our lab, and our test methods, supporting engineers on defined tasks.As you demonstrate judgment, you will take ownership of specific test areas, fixtures, and the calibration program — work that is yours, with your name on it.Strong co-ops are invited back for additional terms with expanded responsibility, and we actively look to convert high performers into full-time engineering or test roles at graduation.You will finish with a portfolio of real work: products you helped validate, fixtures you designed, procedures you wrote, and failures you tracked down. That is experience that transfers anywhere — and we would rather you build it here and stay. QualificationsCurrently pursuing a Bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, or related fieldDemonstrated hands-on experience — coursework labs, senior design, competition teams (IEEE, Robotics, etc.), maker projects, or personal builds. Show us what you have made.Excellent soldering experience, including small components and SMT reworkFoundational understanding of analog and digital circuits. Comfort reading schematics and interpreting datasheets and basic specifications.Careful, methodical work habits. In test engineering, sloppy data is worse than no data, and this role is built on trustworthy measurements.Clear written communication — you will write procedures and failure reports that other people rely on.Familiarity with microcontrollers, embedded systems, and electronics lab equipmentStrong problem-solving skills, curiosity, and a willingness to learn in a hands-on engineering environmentInterest in IoT, connected products, or consumer electronics is a plus The target compensation for the role is $22.00 hour. Why Join Us?At Delta Faucet Company, our people are our greatest assets. We value different perspectives and fostering an inclusive environment. You’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of our brand, working alongside passionate professionals committed to excellence and innovation. Join us to lead progressive growth and make a significant impact within a leading organization.Here are some of the benefits we offer for your personal and professional growth:Culture: Recognized and award-winning reputation for equality, diversity and inclusion, flexibility, work-life balance, and more.Wellbeing: Comprehensive benefit plans; retirement, savings, tuition reimbursement, and employee incentive programs; resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.Learning & Development: LinkedIn Learning access; internal opportunities to work on projects cross-company.Social Impact: Four employee-led and self-directed Business Resource Groups; Paid volunteer day annually; Employees share their time, skills and talent with charities and nonprofit organizations across the U.S. and around the globe. jobs.description: Employer: Jefferies, LLC Expires: 10/23/2026 About JefferiesJefferies is a leading global, full-service investment banking and capital markets firm that provides advisory, sales and trading, research, and wealth and asset management services. Our business technologists enable Jefferies’ sales, trading, research and banking colleagues to solve problems and seize opportunities with more speed and precision than ever before. We deploy and manage the technology that keeps Jefferies running and our colleagues connected. We develop applications and tools to serve Jefferies’ clients and enhance business outcomes with AI and machine learning tools. In an industry being radically reshaped by technology, our IT team is integrated into every facet of Jefferies’ business.An Opportunity to Explore: At Jefferies, you can go where your talents and interests take you. We want curious and creative people eager to push the boundaries of what they can do and passionate about using technology to solve problems and deliver better outcomes for our business.A No Corner Office Culture: Our business technologists work alongside the colleagues they support. This proximity helps technologists understand how the business operates, which data matters, and how to build platforms and applications that create practical value.A Chance to Unlock the Power of Big Data: Our technologists are helping advance cloud computing, native applications, AI and machine learning to translate data into actionable insights, automate functions, strengthen security and make client service more seamless.A Team of Builders and Problem Solvers: Jefferies is growing, entering new markets and regions, and often building technology platforms from the ground up. Technology is central to answering mission-critical questions and delivering the right solution at the right moment.Summer Analyst and Associate Interns may be placed in one of the following teams: Platform Reliability Engineering and Management (PREM), CISO / Information Security, Infrastructure, or Corporate Technology.PLATFORM RELIABILITY ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT (PREM)PREM is responsible for the stability and resiliency of Jefferies’ front-to-back platforms and contributes to service reliability, system resiliency and firm-wide risk mitigation. The team applies Site Reliability Engineering principles across engineering and support, with a focus on automation, toil reduction, capacity management, operational excellence and platform health visibility through enterprise observability. Interns may work across distributed and cloud technologies and gain exposure to application and production support, quality engineering and SRE practices.CISO / INFORMATION SECURITYThe Global Information Security organization protects Jefferies critical systems and sensitive information from internal and external cyber attacks through use of technology as well as efforts such as Cyber Data Analytics. The team develops and maintains security controls, monitoring capabilities, and cyber defense platforms that help safeguard the Firm's technology environment while supporting regulatory and compliance requirements. Information Security professionals work across a broad range of disciplines including cyber engineering, threat detection and response, security operations, identity and access management, vulnerability management, cloud security, data protection, and cyber analytics.INFRASTRUCTUREGlobal Infrastructure builds, operates and maintains the technology backbone that enables Jefferies to function efficiently, securely and reliably. Key areas include networking, telecom and multimedia engineering; desktop, virtualization, messaging, Workplace AI and automation; cloud solutions and platforms; database, Unix, Windows Server and systems engineering; and data centers. The organization also advances cloud adoption, automation, workplace technology and network resiliency. Internship opportunities may include cognitive automation cloud engineering and server automation engineering.CORPORATE TECHNOLOGYCorporate Technology delivers platforms and solutions that support Jefferies’ global operations, including post-trade processing and settlement, enterprise data, compliance and legal technology, regulatory reporting, client onboarding, digitalization and automation, and Finance and HR technology. Interns may work on live projects involving software engineering, data and reporting, cloud platforms, workflow automation, API integrations, and AI/ML while collaborating with engineers, analysts and business partners across the Firm.Equal Employment OpportunityAt Jefferies, we are committed to building a culture that provides opportunities for all employees regardless of our differences and supports a workforce that is reflective of the communities where we work and live. As a result, we are able to pool our collective insights and intelligence to provide fresh and innovative thinking for our clients.Jefferies is committed to creating and sustaining a workforce that welcomes individuals from all backgrounds to apply. Our employment decisions are made without regard to race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, religion, pregnancy, age, medical condition, physical or mental disability, marital status, domestic partner status, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, veteran or military status, genetic information, reproductive health decisions, or any other factor protected by applicable law. We are committed to hiring the most qualified applicants and complying with all federal, state, and local equal employment opportunity laws. As part of this commitment, Jefferies will extend reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities, as required by applicable law.The salary for the Analyst role is $100,000 and Associate role is $120,000 (pro-rated for the 10-week internship program).
